intro.text: MSC is a leading North American distributor of a broad range of metalworking, maintenance, repair and operations (“MRO”) and production fastener and hardware products and services. With more than 80 years of experience, we help customers improve productivity, profitability, and operational performance. We serve individual machine shops, Fortune 1000 companies and manufacturers of all sizes. We also maintain a robust public sector customer base including governments and their instrumentalities such as federal agencies, state governments and public sector healthcare providers. We position ourselves as a mission-critical partner to our customers, offering highly technical and high-touch solutions to solve their most complex challenges.

lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Wages, services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.why: Leases that work like a loan for the asset: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

oi.text: Income from operatio ns increased 6.3% to $320.6 million in fiscal year 2026, as compared to $301.6 million in fiscal year 2025. opex.heading: Operating Expenses
opex.text:
Operating expenses increased 3.5% to $1,266.3 million in fiscal year 2026, as compared to $1,223.6 million in fiscal year 2025. Operating expenses were 31.6% of fiscal year 2026 net sales, as compared to 32.5% for fiscal year 2025. The increase in operating expenses was primarily attributable to higher depreciation and amortization expense, advertising expense and stock-based compensation expense. The decrease in operating expenses as a percentage of net sales was primarily due to growth in net sales outpacing the increase in operating expenses.

Payroll and payroll-related costs were approximately 54.8% of total operating expenses in fiscal year 2026, as compared to 57.0% in fiscal year 2025. Payroll and payroll-related costs, which include salary, incentive compensation, sales commission, and fringe benefit costs, decreased by $3.9 million for fiscal year 2026. Headcount reduction actions during fiscal year 2026 resulted in lower salary and sales commission costs, which were partially offset by our annual merit increase, higher incentive compensation accrual and fringe benefit costs.

Freight expense was $147.2 million for fiscal year 2026, as compared to $150.5 million for fiscal year 2025.
